title: Inside the Circle x Chelsea FC partnership
article_text:
The latest episode of The Game Plan explores why Circle chose Chelsea FC, what brands really want from football sponsorship, and why the strongest partnerships are about far more than logo placement.

Football sponsorship has never been more competitive, yet brands continue to invest heavily in some of the sport’s biggest assets.

On the latest episode of The Game Plan, Anna-Rose Gabbitass sits down with Kash Razzaghi, Chief Commercial Officer at Circle, to discuss the company’s decision to become Chelsea FC’s Principal Partner and front-of-shirt sponsor.

The conversation uses the partnership as a lens to examine a broader question facing the industry: what are brands actually looking for from football sponsorship in 2026?

Razzaghi explains why football’s global reach made it the natural platform for Circle’s ambitions, how the company evaluated one of the most visible sponsorship opportunities in sport, and why Chelsea stood out from the many organisations it considered.

While front-of-shirt sponsorships are often judged on visibility alone, Razzaghi argues that the most effective partnerships are built on much deeper foundations.

“We felt like we were going into this holding hands, jumping in, and we were going to figure things out together,” says Razzaghi.

The episode also explores the growing importance of authentic partnerships, the opportunity presented by both the men’s, women’s and academy games, and why organisations increasingly expect commercial relationships to extend far beyond traditional sponsorship models.

Elsewhere, listeners will hear how Circle plans to measure success in the early stages of the partnership, why the company believes football remains one of the most powerful global marketing platforms, and what the deal could tell us about the future direction of the sponsorship market.

title: CBS adds Spanish-language CONCACAF Champions Cup rights
article_text:
Paramount-owned US broadcaster CBS Sports has consolidated coverage of the CONCACAF Champions Cup regional club tournament, acquiring the Spanish-language rights to add to the English-language rights it already held.

This new deal will run through the 2030 campaign, as will the English-language package, meaning that the Paramount+ OTT streaming service will showcase all 51 CONCACAF Champions Cup games each year in both English and Spanish.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

In addition to Paramount+, select CONCACAF Champions Cup games will air for free in Spanish (and English) on the CBS Sports app.

CBS supplants rival TUDN, the Spanish-language channel in the US owned by Mexican media business TelevisaUnivision, which has broadcast the tournament for a number of years.

The Champions Cup is the region’s premier men’s club competition, featuring the best clubs from North America, Central America, and the Caribbean.

The tournament was established in 1962 and ran in its original incarnation with several format changes through 2008, when it was retitled the CONCACAF Champions League. It then returned to its Champions Cup moniker ahead of the 2024 edition.

Since its inception, the CONCACAF Champions Cup ha been dominated by Mexican sides, who have won all but one of the last 21 editions going back to 2006, and 40 of the 60 editions in all.

Much of the Spanish-speaking community in the US (and indeed the audience for Telemundo) stems from the country’s large Mexican diaspora, which accounts for as much as 11.2% of the population and close to 60% of all Hispanic US citizens.

As such, adding Spanish-language rights to the existing English-language ones, and thus bringing Spanish-language coverage of well-supported Mexican sides like Club America and Tigres to diaspora fans, could bring strong viewership for CBS.

Paramount’s soccer portfolio in the US also includes Europe’s elite UEFA Champions League club competition and rights to the English Football League, the organizer of the second, third, and fourth tiers of the country’s soccer league pyramid.

Earlier this year, CBS Sports landed rights to major competitions organized by the Asian Football Confederation until 2028.

Additionally, it renewed its deal to show Italy’s top-tier Serie A for another season and snapped up England's Women's Super League on a four-year deal.

title: The reason Jack Draper is currently playing tennis in Brazil with Joao Fonseca
article_text:
Jack Draper’s absence from the ATP Tour of late has been an expected one, given all the fitness troubles he’s suffered in recent years.

And, given the specific nature of his current injury, the only real antidote is rest.

For a professional athlete, that is nearly impossible to do, and tennis is arguably even worse.

With no security and a ranking system that benefits the ever-present, Jack Draper has suffered both financially and in terms of his stature: the Brit currently sits outside the world’s top 150.

Who is to blame for Jack Draper’s injury issues?

However, it seems that whatever recovery plan he and his team agreed on has reached its next step, with reports now emerging that he is back on court.

It’s not just reports that have confirmed Draper’s return to on-court action, with photos and videos also surfacing.

The 24-year-old has been pictured training in Rio, Brazil, at the same country club where Joao Fonseca started playing tennis.

In fact, the Brazilian youngster is apparently there now as well, with one update claiming his plan is to ‘get in shape physically and tennis-wise for next year.’

They added: “He also wants to build up his tolerance to high temperatures.”

Fonseca has also ended his season early, as part of a growing list of players struck down by injury. He was seen at the same club on Tuesday, although pictures of him and Draper together remain unreleased.

What is particularly interesting about this decision is not the timing of his return, but where he has chosen to return.

After all, opting to return to practice on clay courts seems odd with the Australian Open likely his ultimate target after taking so long off.

Even if he were to miss that first Grand Slam of the year, the clay-court season does not start until April, assuming he does play any events during the Golden Swing in Brazil and Argentina, across February.

Naturally, the warm weather seems to be his focus, but that could have been achieved on any surface. The clay must have been a conscious choice, and a curious one at that.

title: Alcaraz sails through Shanghai opener, Auger-Aliassime & Fritz also advance
article_text:
The Spanish star, seeded second, put on a dominant show to brush aside the 55th-ranked Argentinian in the second round in just 66 minutes.

"Really, really happy with the way I played today. It wasn't easy," said the 23-year-old former number one.

"Just had two days of preparation... I came from Tokyo, there were totally different conditions," he added. "Just tried to play the best that I can."

Sporting a fresh moustache, Alcaraz signed a camera "Moustache Team" following his win.

Asked by an on-court interviewer about the new look, Alcaraz said: "It's gonna stay."

He will play either Ignacio Buse or Zizou Bergs in the next round.

World number five Felix Auger-Aliassime also survived a scare, needing three hours to beat 77th-ranked Camilo Ugo Carabelli 4-6, 7-6(1), 7-5.

The Canadian will play Spaniard Pablo Carreno-Busta in the third round.

Several matches in the afternoon were suspended due to rain, but Taylor Fritz, Casper Ruud and Arthur Fils all went through as play resumed.

title: The 8 tennis stars ending their season early as Sinner and Swiatek joined by glum Brit
article_text:
The 2026 tennis season is almost over, but some players have decided to end things early and take an extended break. There are just a few tournaments left on the ATP and WTA Tours, including a WTA 500 event in Tokyo and the last Masters 1000 of the men’s season in Paris. All roads lead to the season-ending championships, with the WTA Finals beginning on November 2, while the ATP Finals kick off on November 15.

However, some big names have already ruled themselves out of competition for the rest of 2026. World No. 1 Jannik Sinner has not played a match since July due to a knee injury, and officially brought his season to a close earlier this month. Iga Swiatek joined him earlier this week, pulling out of her last two events with a quad injury. Britain’s Jack Draper made the decision to end his season back in mid-September. Express Sport takes a look at the eight players who have cut things short in 2026…

Sinner has not played a match since he successfully defended his Wimbledon title in July, lifting a fifth Major trophy. The Italian has been battling with a knee injury, which saw him miss the entire North American hard-court swing, including the US Open. He hoped to return in Asia, but pulled out of the ATP 500 event in Beijing and the Shanghai Masters. Then, Sinner finally decided to stop altogether.

“Me, together with the doctors, have decided that I need a course of treatment for my knee, which means that the 2026 season is officially over,” he said in a video announcement. “At the moment, I also need to think about my long-term career. I will do everything possible to get back to 100 per cent.”

The world No. 9 played through a quad injury at last week’s Wuhan Open, but it all got too much. Swiatek was in tears during her semi-final defeat to countrywoman Maja Chwalinska and was seen speaking to her team early in the second set, though she decided against retiring mid-match. She lost 7-5 6-1 and later said she wanted Chwalinska to win in her own right.

Swiatek then travelled to this week’s Ningbo Open but pulled out of the tournament on Tuesday, which meant she could not qualify for the WTA Finals. The Pole later ended her season, meaning she won’t be in action at next week’s WTA 500 event in Tokyo.

“The past few months, or actually the past couple of years, have been incredibly intense and I feel I need to rest and recover my body fully. So that’s exactly what I will do, a bit longer this time. I’ve decided to end my season here, which means I won’t be playing any more tournaments this year,” she wrote on social media.

It’s been a tough 18 months for the Brit, who won Indian Wells in early 2025 and reached a career-high ranking of No. 4 that summer. Since then, he’s been plagued by a bone bruising injury in his left playing arm. A knee injury also saw Draper miss the majority of this year’s clay swing.

The 24-year-old reached the Eastbourne semi-finals in June but then pulled out of Wimbledon one day before his first match. He made a short-lived comeback in Canada and Cincinnati but pulled out of the US Open and, last month, ended his season altogether.

“I am taking this time to reset and heal so when I return I am 100 per cent ready to go. Tennis is my purpose and passion and so when I step back on court I want to make sure that there’s nothing holding me back from where I want to go and achieve the things I know I’m capable of,” he wrote.

Last year, Anisimova reached two Grand Slam finals, won two WTA 1000 titles, and reached the world’s top five. But she was bogged down by a wrist injury in 2026 and brought her season to a close in September.

Announcing the news, the former world No. 3 said: “I will be wrapping up my season for the year. I sustained a wrist injury again, that I need to take care of. Time to get healthy, reset, and see you all in 2027.”

The former world No. 8 took to Instagram to share a lengthy statement, addressing her health challenges in recent years, which caused dizziness and weight loss. Navarro reached a career-high ranking in 2024, making it to the quarter-finals of Wimbledon and the semis of the US Open. But she struggled to back up her results in 2025 and was diagnosed with relative energy deficiency in sport and Hashimoto's hypothyroidism. Navarro admitted to pushing herself, believing it was the right thing to do because she saw results on the tennis court. But she was left feeling fatigued and “angry”.

Now, the American knows her limits and has ended her season early. “I gained some weight this year. But I also gained my life back. I have enough energy to seize every day, to train or compete as hard as I want to, and to live a life outside of tennis,” she wrote. “I am taking the rest of the year to work on dialling in my medication and fueling protocols so that I can hopefully feel back to 100 per cent again.”

title: Falcons, SIT expand partnership to Spanish market ahead of Madrid game
article_text:
Sports Illustrated Tickets (SIT), the ticketing and fan engagement brand that has swept up partnerships across the NFL in recent seasons, has expanded its agreement with the Atlanta Falcons franchise to cover the team’s upcoming international game in Madrid, Spain.

The Falcons will face the Cincinnati Bengals (another SIT partner) at the iconic 84,000-capacity Santiago Bernabeu stadium on November 8, with SIT to serve as the team's official fan experience partner around the game.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Ahead of the fixture, SIT will offer fans the chance to win tickets to the game through a sweepstakes competition.

SIT has been a partner of the Falcons since the beginning of the 2025 season in a fan experience-focused deal that included the creation of the Sports Illustrated Tickets Lounge hospitality space at the team’s Mercedes-Benz Stadium.

Speaking on this new expansion, the vice president of corporate partnerships at Falcons parent AMB Sports and Entertainment, Alex Polofsky, commented: “Sports Illustrated Tickets has been a terrific partner in helping us create memorable experiences for Falcons fans, and we’re excited to extend that relationship internationally as we head to Madrid.

“The NFL’s continued global growth presents incredible opportunities to connect with fans around the world, and this expansion allows us to engage our supporters in Spain in a meaningful way. We look forward to working together to bring the Falcons brand to new audiences and deliver unique opportunities for fans on an international stage.”

SIT is already experienced in the Spanish market, having served as the NFL’s fan engagement partner for its first-ever international game in Madrid in the 2025-26 season.

At that time, SIT chief executive David Lane spoke to Sportcal (GlobalData Sport), explaining: “The game may be held in Madrid, but this is a global event, and a global audience will be tuning in, so it creates increased awareness and opportunities for us as Sports Illustrated Tickets.

“The Spanish market is a focus for us, and we're in active conversations with multiple opportunities and partners there. This [partnership] just helps to start that foundation of what we think is one of the biggest opportunities we see in the world.

“With a partner like the NFL, a stadium [like the Bernabeu], and the team that's responsible for local operations, they are capable of putting on what will be a spectacular game.”

SIT is already an officially licensed NFL ticket vendor through the league’s “open” ticketing system, NFL Ticket HQ.

Recently, it also became the official fan experience partner of the NFL in the UK, in a deal spanning the recent trilogy of London international games.

Having partnered with the league in London this season, and with its partnership with the New England Patriots including the team’s game in Munich, Germany in November, this Spain partnership ensures SIT will feature at five of the six NFL international games in Europe this year.

The Falcons are one of seven NFL teams to partner with SIT, following the New England Patriots, Pittsburgh Steelers, Cincinnati Bengals, Washington Commanders, Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and most recently, the Jacksonville Jaguars.

title: Rafael Nadal leads tributes as star who beat him, Djokovic, Federer & Alcaraz retires from tennis
article_text:
Rafael Nadal, Grigor Dimitrov and Richard Gasquet led the tributes to David Goffin after the Belgian star retired from tennis in Brussels.

In the final match of his career, Goffin was beaten 6-3, 6-4 by world No 37 Alex Michelsen in the second round of the ATP 250 tournament on Thursday.

During an illustrious career, Goffin amassed a 358-276 record and won six ATP Tour titles, while he was a runner-up at the 2017 ATP Finals and the 2019 Cincinnati Masters. He was also a four-time Grand Slam quarter-finalist, and he helped Belgium reach the Davis Cup final in 2015 and 2017.

The 35-year-old reached a career-high ranking of world No 7, which makes him the only Belgian man to be ranked in the top 10.

Goffin earned 21 wins against top 10 players, including multiple victories over Nadal, Carlos Alcaraz and Alexander Zverev, as well as triumphs against Novak Djokovic, Roger Federer and Stan Wawrinka.

Speaking to ATPTour.com after his last match, Goffin said: “I’m proud of all my career. I gave everything to try to reach my goals.

“I’m proud of the attitude that I always had in front of the difficulties that I had in my career. I’m proud of the wins I had, the opponents I beat.

“A lot of things I’m really proud of. But in the end, I have no regrets and I gave everything until the very end.

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

“A younger version of myself would say that it’s quite a good career, quite good emotions with the impressive places that I played, like a stadium with a crowd, the Davis Cup ties that I played. Hopefully a younger David would be impressed.”

After his match with Michelsen, Goffin’s career was celebrated in an on-court ceremony, and tributes recorded by several tennis stars were played on the big screen.

The montage started with a video from 22-time Grand Slam champion Nadal, who had some kinds words for Goffin.

“Hello David. How are you doing, man? I just want to congratulate you on your amazing career,” Nadal said.

“It has been a huge pleasure to share practices, matches, great moments together on the tour.”

Retired French star Gasquet followed Nadal.

“David, this video is to congratulate you in your great career,” the former world No 7 said.

“It has been an honour to share this time with you. You are truly an extraordinary person and an extraordinary player.”

Former world No 3 Dimitrov, who played Goffin 11 times, said: “Congratulations on your incredible career and amazing journey, my dear friend.

“Thank you for sharing the court with me for so many years.”

Goffin extended his career by defeating Remy Bartola 3-6, 6-3, 6-4 in the first round of the European Open on Wednesday.

After battling back from 0-3 down in the third set against Bartola, an emotional Goffin said: “I don’t know what to say, it was one of the toughest moments and nicest moments when I came on the court.

“The first few games were really tough for me with the nerves. Then I started to serve well. Most important is the support that the crowd gave me in the whole match… It is the best feeling we can have.”

Following his last ATP Tour victory, Goffin admitted he had to cancel his plans.

“I’m going to have to cancel the evening I had booked,” Goffin was quoted as saying by L’Equipe.

“It was both the best and the toughest entrance I’ve ever experienced. I was very nervous, and the most important thing was the support of the crowd from the first point to the last.

“Finishing the match with a winning shot was huge. Everything was perfect.”

title: Carlos Alcaraz adds another ATP tournament to 2027 calendar despite schedule complaints
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz has been very vocal about his displeasure at the gruelling nature of the ATP Tour since returning to action after his wrist injury.

The star missed four and a half months of action between April and August, before he made his return at the 2026 US Open.

Since, he’s opened up about playing less tournaments going forward to combat the hectic tennis schedule and his fitness worries.

At the Shanghai Masters, Alcaraz said: “One of the reasons we had to see the players who are getting injured, they [ATP officials] are pushing us too much out of the line sometimes to play a lot of tournaments, to play a lot of matches.

“It’s getting in the wrong direction,” he continued before turning his attention towards Jannik Sinner’s decision to end his season early. “I just wish Jannik the best for these months, just to be in good shape for the next season.”

Despite Alcaraz’s complaints, the Spaniard has added yet another ATP 500 tournament to his growing calendar.

Alcaraz is already confirmed for the Rotterdam Open in February and now he has been confirmed to play Queen’s in London during the grass court swing.

Queen’s is one of the tournaments Alcaraz was forced to miss due to his wrist injury and he has a very good record at the tournament.

The Spaniard has lifted the title at Queen’s on two occasions, in 2023 and 2025, and he has only every suffered one defeat at the London event.

That came against Jack Draper in 2024, who beat the Spaniard in straight sets in the second round of the tournament.

It should be no surprise that Alcaraz has already bolstered his grass court schedule for 2026, where he is also basically guaranteed to play Wimbledon.

Alcaraz has built a superb record on grass over the years, despite playing a limited amount of the surface.

He holds an incredible 35-4 record on the surface since his debut, which equates to a magnificent 90% winning rate on grass.

That’s helped him win Wimbledon twice, in 2023 and 2024, and reached a further final in 2025. The only player to beat Alcaraz in the last four years at Wimbledon is Jannik Sinner, who won the 2025 final against the Spaniard.

As for Queen’s, the ATP 500 tournament was won by Francisco Cerundolo in 2026 in the absence of Alcaraz, who beat Tommy Paul in the London final.

Next year’s Queen’s event is set to take place between the 5th and the 20th June, with the men’s tournament taking place in the second week of action.

title: Midnite secures snooker Triple Crown with UK Championship sponsorship
article_text:
The sportsbook and casino operator now sponsors all three of snooker’s top global tournaments.

Midnite has added the UK Championship to its snooker sponsorship portfolio, meaning it now has partnerships with each of the sport’s top three events.

The casino and sportsbook operator initially partnered with the World Championship in 2025 before adding the Masters to its roster.

The company’s extended agreement with the World Snooker Tour now includes a betting and casino partnership with the third Triple Crown event.

The deal starts in the current season, with the UK Championship held between November 28 and December 6 at the Barbican in York, England.

Callum Wilson, senior PR manager at Midnite, said: "Snooker has been a fantastic sport for us to be involved with, and we're really excited to be extending our partnership with the World Snooker Tour to cover all three Triple Crown events.

“We've already had some great experiences working with WST through the World Championship and the Masters, so adding the UK Championship feels like a natural next step for us.

"These are the three tournaments that every snooker player dreams of winning, and they mean a huge amount to fans as well. To have Midnite involved in all three is something we're really proud of.

"We've enjoyed building our relationship with WST and we're excited to keep that going, finding new ways to get involved in the sport and bring fans closer to the action."

Midnite continues to ramp up its promotional activity, with its snooker expansion the latest deal after a deal with the NFL in the UK and Ireland.

The operator also has a strong presence in UK football, with the likes of Wolverhampton Wanderers.

title: Two Circles Appoints Media Rights Veteran Augustine Tan to Lead APAC Expansion
article_text:
Global sports and entertainment agency Two Circles has officially appointed industry veteran Augustine Tan as Head of Media Rights for the Asia-Pacific (APAC) region, targeting an aggressive commercial expansion across one of the world’s most dynamic media landscapes.

Announced on Tuesday, 20 October 2026, the strategic hire comes as Two Circles looks to bolster its regional rights business, combining audience data analytics, streaming capabilities, and live production assets to assist rights holders in unlocking greater commercial returns from their broadcast content.

Tan brings over two decades of senior sports media rights experience to the role. He previously held high-profile leadership positions at SPORTFIVE, WWE, and Perform/DAZN, overseeing commercial distribution and rights partnerships for tier-one sports properties including FIBA, the WTA, and the NFL. Most recently, Tan operated his own independent sports media consultancy, A Side Project 2022, advising high-profile clients such as World Rugby, Dentsu, and LFCTV on regional distribution strategies.

In his new position, Tan will lead Two Circles’ media rights operations across APAC, driving revenue growth across diverse markets, platforms, and fan bases. The executive appointment builds on the agency’s growing global momentum, following its recently secured partnership extension with the International Skating Union (ISU).

Highlighting the scale of the commercial opportunity across the region, Tan emphasised the role of data-driven insights in capturing market share.

“APAC is one of the most exciting and diverse sports media markets in the world, with huge opportunities for rights holders to grow audiences and unlock new commercial value,” Augustine Tan said. “As the global Fan Economy surges towards $2 trillion, those opportunities are only growing. What attracted me to Two Circles is the ability to approach those opportunities differently. By bringing together media rights expertise, audience intelligence, production and streaming capabilities, my focus is on helping sports organisations build stronger distribution strategies, reach more fans and ultimately drive greater returns from their content.”

Two Circles Chief Executive Officer and Co-Founder Gareth Balch highlighted that integrating audience analytics into rights transactions is essential for modern sports properties aiming to maximise commercial value.

“The way media organisations create value from sports media rights is improving. We are seeing the value of audiences and analytics at the heart of transactions,” Gareth Balch said. “Media rights are growing and the opportunity for our approach is particularly exciting in APAC, where markets, platforms and fan behaviours vary enormously. Augustine brings a brilliant combination of experience and has the relationships and to support our clients to know fans best. We’re excited to have him leading our ambitions in the region as we continue to grow our clients’ global media rights businesses.”

The appointment positions Two Circles to capture broader regional market share as rights holders seek sophisticated, data-driven distribution models across the rapidly changing Asia-Pacific broadcast ecosystem.

title: College Sports Media Rights Bill Awaits House Action
article_text:
Most Division I college athletics programs spend more than they generate, and a new Congressional Research Service (CRS) report examines whether Congress should intervene in college sports media rights, conference realignment and production facility funding, or leave colleges to govern themselves.

The U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) found that 94% of Division I schools, 330 of 352, spent more on athletics than they generated in revenue in the 2023–2024 academic year.

The Protect College Sports Act of 2026, sponsored by Sen. Ted Cruz (R-TX), passed the Senate on Sept. 28.

Football Bowl Subdivision (FBS) schools collectively spent $13.06 billion on athletics in 2025 and generated $13.03 billion in revenue, according to the Knight-Newhouse College Athletics Database. GAO estimated that Power Four college sports media rights revenue of $2.3 billion in 2023–2024 was nearly as large as the combined athletics revenue of all other Division I colleges, at $3.1 billion. That concentration shapes the report's central policy question: whether a statutory antitrust exemption would let schools bargain collectively and stabilize finances, or whether federal intervention would introduce new complications.

The report traces the current structure to NCAA v. Board of Regents of the University of Oklahoma, 468 U.S. 85 (1984), in which the Supreme Court held that the NCAA's television rights policies violated Section 1 of the Sherman Antitrust Act of 1890. Since that ruling, Power Four conferences have used a "granting of rights" model, under which member schools sign their media rights over to the conference in exchange for a share of revenue.

The Protect College Sports Act, as amended by Sen. John Thune's substitute amendment, would create a "covered entity" with an antitrust exemption to collectively negotiate college sports media rights, if schools voluntarily join and the entity includes at least 75% of FBS schools. Title III of the bill would authorize $180 million annually for fiscal 2027 through fiscal 2032 for competitive grants to help historically Black colleges and universities invest in broadband, media production and sports broadcasting infrastructure.

The report also notes that scheduling a College Football Playoff game on the second Saturday of December would conflict with Executive Order 14396, signed March 20, which directs that no postseason college football game be broadcast in a way that directly conflicts with the Army-Navy Game; a provision in the bill as amended would codify that protection in statute.

The Senate passed S. 4668 on Sept. 28 by a 77–22 vote. The House held the bill at the desk on Oct. 5. Unresolved questions include whether the 75% membership threshold is achievable and how a free local telecast requirement might affect media payments.

The report notes that the true costs of college sports may be higher than current estimates, because the expenses tracked by Knight-Newhouse and GAO may not reflect capital expenditures schools incur to meet media production requirements.

title: Dissolved PREM Rugby club set for return after major update
article_text:
London Irish have moved a step closer to a long-awaited return to professional rugby after a major announcement confirmed the future of the club’s name and identity.

In a club statement, it has been revealed that new owners Gamechanger Investments Limited have acquired the club’s name, brand and associated intellectual property in a deal for an undisclosed fee.

The move marks a significant milestone for the club, which was founded in 1898, as preparations continue for a potential comeback.

PREM Rugby has already made clear its ambition to expand the league under its new franchise system.

London Irish could be strong contenders for a place given their history, established fanbase and London location.

They became the third Gallagher Premiership side to go out of business in an eight-month period, following Worcester Warriors and Wasps.

Worcester have since returned to Champ Rugby and won the title in May after finishing fourth in the regular season.

Wasps, meanwhile, remain outside the professional game, with the club currently operating at amateur level.

There had been hope of an Irish revival in February 2025, when a consortium led by former Formula 1 team owner Eddie Jordan bought the club out of administration.

However, Jordan's death just weeks later dealt a major blow to those plans, leaving the club's future uncertain once again.

A formal launch is expected in December 2026 or January 2027, with work continuing behind the scenes to establish the structures needed for a return.

Any comeback will still depend on approval from the relevant governing bodies and competition organisers.

The club have yet to confirm where they would play their home matches. However, chief executive Jamie Balls MBE has indicated that an announcement on the venue will follow in due course.

title: Fiji pitches pride over money in bid to lure Nawaqanitawase
article_text:
MELBOURNE, Oct 23 - Fiji has no chance of matching the financial rewards Australia can offer Mark Nawaqanitawase but the nation's rugby union hopes the lure of representing his ancestral homeland will persuade the dual international to wear the Flying Fijians jersey at next year's World Cup.

With Nawaqanitawase weighing up his international future, Fiji Rugby Union Chairman John Sanday made an emotional pitch to the former Wallabies winger in an interview with Reuters, stressing identity, belonging and the opportunity to inspire a small Pacific nation.

"We will never be able to offer the financial and the marketing rewards that playing for the Wallabies would offer Mark, but we would offer something that goes deeper," Sanday said.

"It's about identity. It's about who we are, and we are Fijians.

"We come from a tiny little island, a speck in the vast Pacific Ocean, but we are punching above our weight in the global rugby hemisphere."

Nawaqanitawase finished up his spell with the Sydney Roosters after his tries helped them to the National Rugby League title earlier this month and is returning to the 15-man game on a two-year deal with Japanese club Wild Knights.

Wallabies coach Les Kiss is keen to secure Nawaqanitawase for the World Cup but the winger declined to be part of the team's squad for the Nations Championship tests and said he would not make a decision until next year.

The 26-year-old, who also has Italian heritage, told a podcast this week that the chance of success in his next endeavour was a bigger motivator than money.

"I still have more to prove. I don't know where that's going to be, but wherever I go, I feel like I have a lot to give the team," he told 'The Good, the Bad & the Rugby' podcast.

"Whoever it's for, I want to go and win it."

Nawaqanitawase also spoke warmly of his Fijian upbringing, recalling a household buzzing with visiting Fijian relatives and annual school holiday trips to his ancestral village.

"I grew up in the village running around playing touch, whether it was with a coconut or a bottle, playing volleyball or just swimming in the river," he said.

Sanday said those connections could prove decisive in his next move.

"He is one of us. He's a Fijian. He has a village where his father is from. He has a tribe and a clan to where he belongs," he said.

"Yes, he's Australian. We respect that, and if he chooses to go for Australia, of course, we will always respect that. I'd say that we would like to see him come and just play a year for us, and then he can go back to the Aussies." REUTERS

title: Brodie Retallick provides latest update on All Blacks future with Dave Rennie 'throwing it out there'
article_text:
Brodie Retallick refuses to be tempted by Dave Rennie and insists that his All Blacks career is over despite ploughing on in the club game.

The legendary lock has stated that he will continue his career beyond the next Rugby World Cup but that it will not be at Test level, unless there are changes to NZ Rugby’s overseas policy.

Retallick last featured for New Zealand in the 2023 World Cup final but Rennie was open about wanting to bring him back.

However, the 35-year-old is very content in Japan and has made peace with the fact that he will not put on the black jersey again.

Asked on the Sportscafe Legends podcast whether Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour made him miss playing for the All Blacks he responded: “Not anymore.”

Retallick then added: “After the World Cup, maybe it was the way of losing the final in France, the year or two after that, I would sit there and watch the ABs and say to myself, ‘could I still do it? Am I still good enough?’

“I think enough time’s passed now and I was happy when I did leave. I felt like I left on my own terms, which I was pretty happy about.

“Dave Rennie was here coaching the last couple of years and he threw it out there a few times about coming back, but I think my time’s done.”

Retallick was pressed on whether he is thinking about the World Cup in Australia, which starts in just under a year’s time, the Kobe Steelers second-row’s response was once again blunt.

“Not really, no,” he said. “I haven’t really considered it. Until they change the rules, it’s not even a possibility, so I’m not even going to entertain it.

“I’m 35 now, I’ve got this season and one more on my Kobe contract and I think that will probably be it for me.”

Despite saying the 2027/28 season may well be his last, Retallick did then open up the possibility of joining a team in Europe or the USA.

“I thought I would be done by now. I had some plans and life changes but I would like to see these couple of seasons out and, who knows, maybe try a stint in an Italy or an America, just for the life experience, and then head back to the Bay,” he said.

“I don’t know if coaching is for me. I’ve learned a lot of things with techniques and styles over the years, and whether to be involved in younger grade rugby to try and influence some people, but I’m more of a fly by the seat of my pants, and when it happens it happens, so we will work it out when we get there.”

Part of the reason Retallick has ruled out playing for the All Blacks is his love of playing in Japan. Having also spent two years at Kobe between the 2019 and 2023 World Cups, Retallick is now set for his sixth season at the club.

“It’s awesome,” he said. “Probably off the field is just as much as a highlight than on the field. The way we play at Kobe is completely different to a lot of the Japan teams.

“We will attack from anywhere on the field pretty much, if we see the space, probably hence why we score so many tries.

“Last year in particular we got the balance right and we won a League One title, the first time I’ve won here in eight years, so it was pretty special to be a part of that.

“I’ve been the captain the last three seasons so I was pretty chuffed as a foreigner to come over here and earn a little bit of their respect and lead them to a title. It’s not something everyone gets to do.”

title: Arthur Blank adds women's golf team to sports portfolio with Atlanta Drive GC
Nick Faldo on LIV Golf: "Sport must have consequences"
article_text:
For Nick Faldo, the problem with LIV Golf isn't the money, but what's missing: the fear of failure. In late August, the six-time major champion spoke on the "Sky Sports Golf Podcast" about the future of the league. His reasoning went to the heart of the format. Today, nearly two months later, LIV is in the middle of bankruptcy proceedings, and several stars have left the league.

LIV's season finale provided the occasion for the conversation. The team finale in Michigan had been cancelled, and the tournament in Indianapolis became the final event of the 2026 season. There, rookie Michael La Sasso won with 18 under par, one stroke ahead of Jon Rahm. The 22-year-old became the youngest winner in LIV history.

Faldo shared what he heard "at the back of the range": other team captains had wrapped up with their teams, and in the end, more players wanted to leave LIV than join it. He doubted that anyone would seriously invest large sums in a product that doesn't resonate with the public.

But the sporting core was more important to him. Faldo recalled a documentary about Rafael Nadal, which showed that without overcoming adversity, no great champions are born. That's exactly what LIV lacks.

"Sport must have consequences. There must be a certain element of fear in sport. To me, it's as if you can't fail at all. And that's not sport."

Faldo has been advocating for the importance of the cut for years. When even the world number one misses the cut line on Friday, real drama unfolds for him. The player is then half embarrassed and must still struggle with a game that isn't working that day. There is no cut at LIV events.

Faldo recalled his own career: he made his Open debut 50 years ago, in 1977 he competed in his first Ryder Cup. The best tournaments in the world have been, and still are, the four majors and the Ryder Cup, plus about 20 other top events. They're played over 72 holes, with real consequences and plenty of history. Gimmicks like music on the range or cannon starts don't change that. His conclusion:

"Money is not the highest thing in sport. It's about competition, about passion, about the fear of failure. That's sport," Faldo said.

Recent developments align in many ways with Faldo's assessment. In September, LIV Golf filed for bankruptcy under Chapter 11. The Saudi sovereign wealth fund PIF is ending its funding after the 2026 season. The new backer is BC Partners, which wants to invest up to 300 million dollars in a new version with ten tournaments starting in 2027. Players must decide by October 25.

Many have already made their decision. Jon Rahm will not be part of LIV 2.0. Sergio Garcia was released from his contract in court. David Puig, Abraham Ancer, and Adrian Meronk have also left the league. Many are drawn back to established tours, where they find again what Faldo has been missing: a Friday where everything can be at stake.

Source of quotes: "Sky Sports Golf Podcast", episode from 08/25/2026.

title: The state of the game: key takeaways from IFR’s inaugural report on English football
article_text:
The State of the Game (SotG) report published on 13th October 2026 is the IFR’s first major output. The 245-page report sets out the regulator’s assessment of the financial health of the game and provides an early indication of how interventionist it may be in applying its licensing powers. As a draft publication, the IFR must consider any responses before issuing its final report by May 2027.

The report sets out the IFR’s view that English football is in poor financial health at all levels of the game. It considers that a new package of financial support is needed to sustain the football pyramid. This must be accompanied by action that will reduce financial risk, but changes should not undermine the success of the game.

Growth: Football, particularly the Premier League, has been excellent at driving revenue growth, with huge amounts of inward investment. The UK£9 billion of revenue in English football in 2025/2026 is far higher than any comparable market.

Lack of cost control: Despite strong revenue growth, an inability to control wages means 94 per cent of clubs are loss making and under severe financial pressure. This is because clubs continue to spend heavily on players to improve on and off-field performance and grow their enterprise value.

Financial cliff edges: One contributor to wage inflation is the cliff edges between divisions, where a promotion leads to a big jump in prize money, broadcasting, and commercial revenue. This incentivises overspending and excessive risk taking, as clubs chase the financial rewards on offer from progression through the leagues. Equally, relegation can be catastrophic to a club’s long -term financial health, as revenue drops sharply.

For the complete list of key findings and insights – covering debt, owner reliance and redistribution – download the report here.

title: Exeter's Wyatt suffers fresh injury blow
article_text:
Exeter back Tommy Wyatt could be out until December after injuring his ankle.

It is the latest problem for the 26-year-old, who returned from a serious knee injury this summer, only to damage his shoulder in the final game of pre-season.

Wyatt came off in the first half of Exeter's European Champions Cup loss at Toulouse having played Exeter's previous three games.

It add more pressure to Exeter's strained backs division ahead of Saturday's Prem game at Bristol (17:30 BST).

Winger Campbell Ridl is out for the season, England's Immanuel Feyi-Waboso has a hamstring issue while Paul Brown-Bampoe and Olly Woodburn are also injured.

"The initial prognosis is it's not operable," Exeter director of rugby Rob Baxter told BBC Sport.

"So he should be back either late in the Prem Cup period or as we get back into the Premiership hopefully if things go well.

"It was another significant injury to a back three player which we seem to be we seem to be stacking up pretty quickly.

"You've got to feel for him, but it's part of the game now and you've kind of got to get on with it."

title: Dudeney wins epic as British trio march on in Wrexham
article_text:
Alicia Dudeney led a great day for British players on day three of the Lexus Wrexham Open as she joined Jodie Burrage and Hannah Klugman in progressing to Friday's quarter-finals.

The in-form Dudeney extended her winning run to seven matches in the World Tennis Tour W100 event at Wrexham Tennis and Padel Centre, outlasting seventh seed Susan Bandecchi from Switzerland 6-3 6-7 (4-7) 6-4 in a match lasting two hours and 51 minutes.

She will now face French player Elsa Jacquemot in the last eight.

Dudeney was followed into the Carden Park Arena by Klugman, with the 17-year-old producing another excellent performance to beat higher ranked Czech player Anna Siskova 6-2 6-4.

Klugman, who reached the French Open junior girls' final last year and is currently ranked 341, will now play sixth seed Rebecca Sramkova from Slovakia.

Watch live on BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport website and app.

Burrage ensured there would be three British players in action on Friday by beating fourth seed Noma Noha Akugue 6-1 7-6 (11-9).

She will next play Marina Bassols Ribera, the fifth seed, following the Spanish star's victory over Australian Lizette Cabrera.

There was a big upset elsewhere as top seed Anna Blinkova, the French player currently 72 in the world rankings, fell at the second-round stage as she lost 6-3 6-2 against Suzan Lamens from the Netherlands.

The form of the British trio has helped bolster home fans after reigning champion Mimi Xu, from Swansea, opted not to defend her title this year, instead competing at the W75 Saguenay tournament in Canada.

title: Welsh rugby player faces calls for life ban as vile act makes global headlines
article_text:
Calls are growing for a lifetime ban to be dished out following a horror incident in the match between Llandovery and Ebbw Vale on Thursday night.

In the first half of the Super Rygbi Cymru at Church Bank, Ebbw Vale's Curtis Gregory was given a straight red card for a stamp on opposition player Joe Powell which left viewers appalled by its ferocity.

With a ruck formed, Powell briefly held onto Gregory's leg, which prompted him to stamp down on the former's outstretched limb with significant force.

Luckily for the stricken player, he appeared to escape without visible injury and quickly made his feelings clear to Gregory by shoving him backwards.

The Welsh Rugby Union is currently awaiting the official's report beofre a disciplinary panel will consider the case and sanctions.

Referee Craig Evans stopped play immediately in the 35th minute and, telling Ebbw Vale's captain: "We have a stamp by this player. I did ask the question if anything aggravated it. My AR (assistant referee) didn't see anything. It's a stamp on the leg. Red card. Permanent."

The game was being shown live by S4C and replays of the incident drew groans from the Welsh language commentators.

Footage of the flashpoint quickly circulated online and news has spread around the world, with major news sites in South Africa and Australia generating headlines on it. News.com.au led with the item overnight "Rugby shocked by 'most vindictive' foul play as furious fans call for lifetime ban".

Discourse online has already seen calls grow for the most severe punishment.

"Difficult to know how long to ban Curtis Gregory for here. But it has to be long. Very long," one commentator said. "Unbelievably thick and very dangerous," added another.

"One of the worst I’ve seen watching rugby for nearly 40 years. Should never step on the field again," offered up a third.

"Reminds me of that 1995 stamp on Doddie Weir. All of the books will be thrown. Long ban incoming," said rugby journalist Andy McGeady.

"Yeah that’s a lifetime ban. That’s actually p***** me off, one of the scummiest things I’ve seen on a rugby pitch," volunteered another viewer.

Despite going 15-0 down and being reduced to 13 men at one stage, Ebbw rallied to win the match 31-15 with 31 unanswered points.

title: “Unfinished business” – Jonny Wilkinson opens up on rugby return
article_text:
England legend Jonny Wilkinson has opened up about his rugby journey, admitting he still has “unfinished business” 15 years after his international retirement.

The 2003 World Cup hero shared an emotional message with fans on Thursday.

And it seems the man with the most famous left boot in English rugby still has plenty to give.

Wilkinson, now 47, has been sharing more of his rugby knowledge through coaching sessions and social media videos.

From kicking tips to detailed breakdowns, the former England fly-half remains as keen on the sport as ever.

Wilkinson shared two photos from the 2011 Rugby World Cup, his last tournament with England.

He also admitted his international career did not finish as he had hoped.

“I retired from international rugby 15 yrs ago. It didn’t end the way I hoped.”

But the next part of his message caught the eye.

“But where there is still passion, there is unfinished business.”

The former Toulon star added that he still had plenty to discover about himself.

“Performance and finding out what I’m capable of is my life purpose.”

He also stressed that his drive remains just as strong away from the pitch.

Wilkinson may have hung up his boots, but his love for rugby has never faded.

In January, the World Cup winner returned to his boyhood club Farnham RFC to help coach the next generation.

The session saw him share the skills and habits that made him one of rugby's greatest kickers.

It wasn't his first taste of coaching, either.

Back in 2024, Wilkinson worked with England's coaching staff, helping Marcus Smith and Fin Smith prepare for the summer Tests.

And anyone who remembers his famous training habits will hardly be shocked.

This was a man who made an art form out of staying behind after training.

Wilkinson has also been showing fans that his famous left boot still works.

The former fly-half casually sent a rugby ball through a basketball hoop.

England cricket star Jonny Bairstow was among those left impressed.

The video was another reminder that class is permanent.

Now, rather than landing match-winning kicks himself, Wilkinson is passing on his knowledge.

Whether that leads to a bigger coaching role remains to be seen.

Jonny Wilkinson still isn't finished with rugby.

1. He was just 18 when he made his England debut

Wilkinson made his England debut against Ireland in 1998.

He was just 18 years old and went on to win 91 caps for his country.

2. His famous World Cup kick came with his weaker foot

Wilkinson's winning drop goal against Australia in 2003 came from his right foot.

That's right. One of rugby's most famous left-footed kickers won the World Cup with his weaker foot.

3. He scored more than 1,200 points for England

Wilkinson finished his England career with 1,179 Test points.

Add his six British and Irish Lions points, and his international total rises to 1,185.

4. He won the European Cup twice with Toulon

Wilkinson joined Toulon in 2009 and helped turn the French club into a European powerhouse.

He lifted the Heineken Cup in both 2013 and 2014 before retiring from professional rugby.

Wilkinson was awarded an MBE in 2003 and an OBE in 2004.

He was later made a CBE in the 2015 New Year Honours for services to rugby union.

Steve Borthwick has some big calls to make ahead of England's autumn campaign.

Would you stick with the tried and tested stars or give some fresh faces a chance?

Now it's your turn to play England boss.

title: All Blacks injury list: 18 players facing fitness concerns ahead of Nations Championship
article_text:
The All Blacks have been hit by a brutal run of injuries ahead of November's Nations Championship, with 18 players suffering setbacks or facing recent fitness concerns.

Dave Rennie has already lost six players for the northern tour. Several more are fighting to get fit.

And some of the biggest names in New Zealand rugby are on the list.

The bad news? Their treatment room is getting rather crowded.

Here is the latest injury picture ahead of Tests against Scotland, Wales and England.

The All Blacks captain suffered a dislocated shoulder during the series against South Africa.

Savea required surgery and will miss the northern tour.

His absence is a huge blow for Rennie, who has turned to Codie Taylor for leadership.

The powerful winger suffered a ruptured shoulder tendon.

Initial medical reports suggested Clarke would miss around five months.

That rules him out of the November Tests.

Jacobson underwent surgery after suffering an elbow tendon injury.

His recovery was initially expected to take four to five months.

The back-row forward will not feature in November.

Love suffered ankle ligament damage during the series against South Africa.

The talented playmaker requires surgery and is out for the rest of 2026.

His absence has left Rennie short of options at fly-half.

The prop suffered a knee cartilage injury.

New Zealand Rugby initially expected Norris to return during the Super Rugby pre-season.

Carter is the latest player to join the injury list.

The winger suffered a high ankle injury while scoring against Australia at Eden Park.

He has since undergone surgery and will miss the Nations Championship Northern Series.

Mo'unga suffered a calf tear during training before the Bledisloe Cup.

Rennie suggested the fly-half could face six to eight weeks out.

That puts his involvement in November in serious doubt.

Barrett missed the second Bledisloe Cup Test after suffering calf tightness.

The injury failed to settle in time for the match in Sydney.

New Zealand will hope the centre recovers before the tour.

Frizell suffered a knee injury during the 43-21 victory over Australia.

The forward required further medical checks.

His availability for November remains uncertain.

The hooker was another casualty of the Sydney victory.

He left the field with calf tightness and was due to undergo a scan.

Rennie will be hoping the issue is minor.

Tupaea was forced off early against Australia after suffering a concussion.

The centre must complete the required return-to-play process.

His availability will depend on medical clearance.

Jordan was withdrawn during the second Bledisloe Cup Test.

The outside back was struggling with calf tightness.

His withdrawal was described as precautionary, offering some hope ahead of November.

Blackadder missed the second Test against Australia with a calf injury.

The hard-working forward has endured another frustrating fitness setback.

Aumua was unavailable for the Sydney Test due to concussion.

The hooker must pass the required medical checks before returning.

Segner was also ruled out of the second Bledisloe Cup Test.

The loose forward was listed as unavailable due to concussion.

His return depends on medical clearance.

Fineanganofo suffered a hamstring injury while playing for Bay of Plenty.

He also sustained a concussion in the same match.

The Newcastle Red Bulls-bound winger faces a race to regain full fitness.

Proctor suffered a fractured shoulder blade during the South Africa tour.

His initial recovery period was estimated at four to six weeks.

That could put him in contention for November, although his fitness needs confirming.

The experienced lock was unavailable for the Bledisloe Cup squad due to a calf injury.

His recovery will be watched closely before Rennie names his northern tour squad.

New Zealand face a tough trip north, with Nations Championship matches against Scotland, Wales and England in November.

The All Blacks will then take part in the Nations Championship Finals Weekend in London.

Rennie has already shown he can cope without several established stars.

But with six players definitely out and others facing fitness tests, his next squad announcement could make interesting reading.

French Open: Unheralded Heroes Shine
article_text:
Several big names saw their campaigns come to an end in the YONEX French Open 2026 second round as lesser-fancied contenders made their mark on Thursday.

Marvin Seidel/Thuc Phuong Nguyen were among the day’s standout performers, reaching the quarterfinals with a 21-17 14-21 21-19 victory over in-form world No.2 duo Jiang Zhen Bang and Wei Ya Xin.

The result continues a remarkable run in Paris for the Germans, who have now beaten two top 10 pairs; they ousted world No.9s Goh Soon Huat/Lai Shevon Jemie in the first round.

Jiang/Wei arrived in France having won consecutive titles (Arctic and Denmark Opens) but Seidel and Nguyen refused to be overawed by their lofty ranking.

“It’s one of our best wins so far,” said Nguyen. “We can play against them. We had to not hide and be really brave.”

For Seidel, the run is about more than results alone.

“This is huge. It’s very important for German badminton that everyone sees we are still there, that we are trying our best and all the youth players also see we can do that. We are really happy about that and we want to keep going.”

The world No.27s now face Hoo Pang Ron/Lai Pei Jing for a place in the semifinals.

Another player enjoying a memorable week is Ashmita Chaliha, who claimed the biggest victory of her career – a 21-19 21-18 win over world No.3 Akane Yamaguchi – to reach her maiden Super 750 quarterfinal.

Having lost to Yamaguchi just a week earlier in Denmark, Chaliha had a different mindset in Paris.

“I had no hopes or expectations. She’s a legend, I was just looking forward to giving my best and everything else would follow.”

The world No.36 drew confidence from her previous encounter and was better prepared to deal with one of Yamaguchi’s most dangerous shots.

“Her deceptive drop is very effective and difficult to take. Today I was ready for her drops as well,” said the 27-year-old.

“This is my biggest win. I’m still trying to digest it. I think it will take a day. This is my first 750 quarterfinal and I’m super proud of myself and how I played here.

“I watch men’s singles as inspiration for my style. I really like Lin-Chun Yi. He’s lefthanded like me and explosive.”

Chaliha’s reward is a meeting with another Japanese, former world champion Nozomi Okuhara, who beat eighth seed Pornpawee Chochuwong 16-21 29-27 21-12.

Other favourites to fall on Thursday were women’s singles No.2 seed Wang Zhi Yi and men’s singles fifth seed Chou Tien Chen. Wang was shown the door by Hina Akechi while Chou succumbed to teammate Chi Yu Jen.

“It’s an exciting moment. I took some lessons from losing to her at the All England. Now I want to think about how to prepare for my next match,” said Akechi after her 21-19 22-20 win.

title: PGA Tour pro names biggest change he's happiest about with 2028 schedule
article_text:
Long-time PGA Tour pro Joel Dahmen has welcomed the sweeping changes planned for 2028 but believes veterans could face an uphill battle to remain competitive.

The North American circuit is moving to a two-tier structure in two years' time, with the introduction of a Championship and Challenger Series.

Players will switch level at the end of the season based on performance. Golfers who win twice on the second tier will earn automatic promotion.

The new model was approved by the Tour's policy board in June and is designed to keep the world's leading players together more consistently and increase the consequence of poor performance.

PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp, who will take over as commissioner from Jay Monahan at the end of the year, also believes that fans will also have a clearer season-long storyline.

Dahmen told FrontOfficeSports in a recent Q&A that the biggest thing he's happy with is clarity, adding: "It's defined what the future looks like, it's defined what your number is.

"Because even this past year for me, [I] started off with some conditional status, but played well enough, that got me into signature events, got to play Bay Hill, I played the Players.

"And then a couple weeks later I wasn't getting into fields that were like regular events. So it was just kind of up and down and all over the place.

"And I think at least going forward, you know where you're going to play, you know what your schedule is going to be, and you know what you need to do to get to the next level, you know, to get up to that championship series.

"So, I don't have a problem with it. I'm just glad that we know what we're doing."

Dahmen said he hopes to play at the top level for at least five or six more years.

"I think this affords me, you know, a definite opportunity to do that," he said.

One of the biggest criticisms of the PGA Tour in recent years is that too many playing opportunities are awarded to veteran players.

Before the 2025 campaign, the number of fully exempt cards on offer was 125. This has been reduced to 100.

Dahmen believes the growing strength of younger golfers will make it increasingly difficult for older players to hold on to their places.

"I mean, the game of golf is more competitive than it's ever been," he said.

"They're as good as they've ever been, and you have some veterans like myself, you know, trying to hang on as long as possible out there."

title: Padel’s Hexagon World Series reveals inaugural season’s event hosts
article_text:
Padel's first-ever Hexagon World Series (HWS), starting in late January in Madrid, will conclude in Abu Dhabi in October, it has been revealed today.

This comes after the announcement in December last year that the International Padel Federation's Hexagon Cup, originally a team competition backed by a range of global sporting stars, will now turn into a worldwide circuit of events.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Following the series launching in the Spanish capital of Madrid, between January 21 and 24 (to be title sponsored by Generali), it will then head to North America in March and Scandinavia in June, before the four-event season comes to an end with a finale in Abu Dhabi in October.

This was all unveiled at the official launch of the inaugural Hexagon World Series, in Abu Dhabi.

HWS was originally slated to begin in 2026 but was pushed back to next year, which the organizers said was due to “the international scale and ambition of Hexagon World Series, together with the work required to build a robust and sustainable structure across multiple markets.”

The specific countries and cities set to host the North American and Scandinavian events will be unveiled soon, the sport's governing body has said.

Up until this point, the Hexagon Cup – which held its first edition in early 2024 – has been a short single tournament taking place each year in Madrid, but will change, thanks to a partnership struck by the event's organizers with the International Padel Federation (FIP) governing body, and with worldwide sports and entertainment agency 54.

The 54 agency, involved in the creation of the controversial LIV Golf rebel series a few years ago, invested and partnered with Hexagon Cup to launch HWS.

This will become the first team padel series to be launched under the FIP's governance and will be integrated into the body's calendar.

The sport's authorities are currently attempting to boost padel's chances of being included in the Olympic program and will hope that this addition of a top-tier teams-based series is a step towards doing that.

HWS will take place alongside the existing Premier Padel circuit (played by pairs, not teams), and will add multiple events per year across new international locations.

title: 2026 Genesis Championship - Day Two Digest
article_text:
Jarvis and Rozner lead, the battle for a Tour card comes to an emotional end for some, while others keep their hopes alive at Woo Jeong Hills Country Club.

Here's what you need to know from the second round of the Genesis Championship in South Korea.

Antoine Rozner made two birdies in his final three holes to catch first-round leader Casey Jarvis as the pair head into the weekend of the Genesis Championship in a share of the lead.

The South African mixed four birdies with 14 pars to set the clubhouse target with a bogey-free 67, strengthening his bid for a third victory of the season that would lift him to second on the Race to Dubai Rankings Delivered by DP World.

But Rozner produced one of the rounds of the day late in the afternoon to draw level at the halfway stage, carding a flawless six-under 65.Starting on the tenth, the Frenchman rolled in a 44-foot birdie putt at the 13th before adding further gains at the 16th and 18th to reach the turn in 33. He then picked up three more shots with short-range birdie conversions at the fifth, seventh and eighth holes to complete his bogey-free effort.

On a dramatic second day in Korea, there were several players who guaranteed they will have a fighting chance to retain the full playing rights on the DP World Tour for next season.

Yuto Katsuragawa, who is ranked 106th, made a birdie at the last to add a second-round 69 to his opening 67 and move into a share of tenth place heading into the weekend. It moves him into a projected position of 96th, up ten places.

Matteo Manassero (98th) and Sean Crocker (103rd) both made the cut on the number, and will both be targetting a big weekend as they are currently projected to end the season at 99th and 101st respectively.

Elsewhere, Brandon Robinson Thompson (109th) made his own move, with a second round 69 to add to his opening 71. Tied for 26th, he was at one stage on Friday predicted to be 100th, but is currently at 105th.

With the jubilation of retaining cards for some also comes the unavoidable heartache for others who will need to go back to Qualifying School to retain their full status after a missed cut in the final event of the regular season.

Sebastian Söderberg, the man who came in at 101st on the Race to Dubai Rankings Delivered by DP World, was unable to come back from a disappointing opening 76 (+5) to miss the cut nable to improve his position. He is currently projected to finish at 103rd in the standings.

Kiradech Aphibarnrat came into this week with hope of doing enough to keep his card, but after a disappointing opening round, the four-time winnerr was forced to withdraw halfway through his second round with injury to his back and is now projected to be at 110th.

Nine-time DP World Tour winner Pablo Larrazábal also fell short in his bid to retain playing privileges for 2027, bringing to a close a remarkable spell among the Tour's ranks that began when he earned his card in 2007, ending this year projected to finish 166th.

Other players who missed the cut and finished outside the top 100 include Dylan Naidoo and Elvis Smylie, while multiple winner Marcel Siem withdrew after the opening round.

Others, such as David Law and Eddie Pepperell, remain inside the top 100 but face a nervy wait over the weekend.

It undoubtedly belonged to Doyeb Mun, with this hole out eagle at the sixth. The South Korean, who is teeing up in just his fifth start on the DP World Tour, signed for a 67 on day two that has him in a share of 14th.
